The survivor is the theory with higher empirical content that has not yet been falsified; preferring it is rational because it offers the best available approximation to truth without asserting its likelihood.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the concept of verisimilitude is logically incoherent within Popper's own framework (as argued by Tich\u00fd and Miller).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If acting on the 'best bet' implicitly assumes that past survival correlates with future success (uniformity of nature).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 'truth-likeness' cannot be assessed without invoking probabilistic measures of confirmation.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Verisimilitude-based Pragmatism: Popper distinguishes between logical probability (which remains zero or undefined for universal laws) and verisimilitude (closeness to truth). Corroboration reports past performance but serves as a marker for potential verisimilitude. We prefer the better-corroborated theory not because it is more likely true, but because it has survived tests that falsified its rivals, making it the 'best bet' for truth in a landscape where certainty is impossible. This avoids induction by treating the preference as a methodological imperative to seek truth, not a probabilistic inference about the future.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
